newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on squaring-off demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on squaring-off demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed up against the dollar on Thursday as banks scrambled for rupees to cover their requirement for squaring off with the Central Bank, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.95 to the U.S. currency after opening at 57.14. The currency closed at 57.15 on Wednesday.
Overnight call money, which opened at 13.25 percent, shot up later in the day to close at 22 percent, dealers said.
"There was a problem in liquidity today. Banks were stuck for money but there were no lenders," a Hatton National Bank dealer said.
"The rupee went up because people, instead of borrowing high, were trying to convert their dollars to rupees to cover their Central Bank requirement," he said.
Thursday is squaring-off day. Earlier in the day, the Central Bank pushed down the dollar by quarter local cent, and fixed buying and selling prices at 56.2914 and 57.4286.

Dealers expect the market to be liquid on Friday as some four billion rupees arrive in the market, as a result of the Central Bank's dropping of its reserve requirement from 15 to 14 percent, which goes into effect tomorrow.
